summary: DROP proposed (lot-only camping): the brochure says 'Camping is allowed along interior roads and/or parking lots. No amenities provided.' The area has one lot, the boat-ramp lot on its 12-acre lake, and MDC's single GIS camping point (605) sits on that lot's west edge (lot 2196 is 26 m away). No campground, pad or camping area apart from the ramp lot.
flags: DROP (lot-only): brochure https://mdc.mo.gov/sites/default/files/2023-05/9228.pdf: 'Camping is allowed along interior roads and/ or parking lots. No amenities provided. Seasonal closures and restrictions may apply. Stays are limited to 14 consecutive days in a 30-day period.' The area page lists 'Camping: Designated Camping Sites' and the GIS has one point, 605 'Lick Creek Conservation Area Designated Camping Area' at 39.15005,-92.38524 = the stored pin. But that point is the west edge of the area's only lot (GIS 26 lot 2196, 26 m) - the gravel boat-ramp lot at the end of the area drive on 12-acre Lick Creek Lake, ~25 m from the ramp. Imagery shows nothing but the lot and a small gravel bump-out on its west side. The 2019 area map has no camping symbol (legend: parking lot, concrete boat ramp, hiking trail). This is the brochure 'camping permitted in the parking lot' case of the 2026-11-09 rules (as Girvin, 14001).

If kept anyway: Rule 140 standard; no Rule 101; owner MDC; phone 'For more information call (573) 815-7900' matches stored. Waterfront: the point is ~25-40 m from the lake across the ramp lot (a ramp lot is not an open apron) - lakeview at most; the stored lakeview holds. Directions as stored (Hwy 63 north 9 mi, Hwy 124 west 3 mi, Oak Grove School Road north 1.8 mi). Horses: no horse camp or horse use listed. No other entry within 3 km.
